diagnosis: Immortal time bias in an observational cohort
mechanism: Immortal time bias occurs when a period during which an outcome could not have occurred for a participant to be classified as exposed is incorrectly assigned to the exposed group. The guaranteed survival interval before exposure can create a spurious protective association unless exposure is modeled as time-varying or person-time is classified correctly.
vignette: Investigators use hospital records to study whether starting a cardiac rehabilitation program within 30 days after discharge reduces 1-year mortality after myocardial infarction. Patients are classified as 'rehabilitation users' if they attend at least one session within 30 days. All follow-up time beginning on the day of discharge is then assigned to that group, including the days before the first rehabilitation session. Patients who die before attending a session are classified as nonusers. The rehabilitation group has substantially lower observed mortality.
lead: Which of the following biases most directly threatens the validity of this apparent survival benefit?
distractor_notes: Confounding by indication can affect treatment comparisons, but the defining design flaw here is assignment of guaranteed pre-exposure survival time to the exposed group.
Recall bias concerns differential accuracy of remembered past exposures; this study uses recorded dates rather than retrospective self-report.
Nonresponse bias arises when study participation differs systematically between responders and nonresponders; no survey-response mechanism is described.
Lead-time bias concerns earlier diagnosis making survival from diagnosis appear longer without changing time of death; this cohort instead misclassifies pre-exposure person-time.
key_expl: To be classified as a rehabilitation user, a patient must survive long enough after discharge to attend the first session. If the interval from discharge until that session is counted as exposed person-time, it is 'immortal' with respect to death because death during that interval would have prevented membership in the exposed group. This can make rehabilitation appear protective even without a causal benefit. Correct analysis treats rehabilitation exposure as time-varying or assigns person-time according to actual exposure status.
objective: Recognize immortal time bias when guaranteed survival before treatment initiation is incorrectly credited to the treated group in an observational cohort.
clues: patients must survive to receive exposure
pre-exposure time assigned to exposed group
early deaths forced into unexposed group
